newsitem.title: DENMARK: Rocket wrecks Danish police cells in biker gang war.
newsitem.headline: Rocket wrecks Danish police cells in biker gang war.

text.p: An anti-tank missile smashed into a Danish police cellblock on Tuesday, wrecking two cells but leaving unhurt a member of the Bandidos motorcycle gang and another inmate held there.

The attack in Holbaek, 50 km (30 miles) west of Copenhagen, appeared to be the latest blow in a vicious turf war between the Bandidos and Hells Angels biker gangs which has killed eight people so far.

Police in Holbaek said the rocket, fired from a nearby park, struck two cells but did not explode. "One of the two internees had Bandidos connections, I can't say more at this stage," Detective Inspector Christian Petersen said.
"We have located the rocket launching device which closely resembles those used in other similar attacks. Police technicians are inspecting the device," he said.

Police said the missile, made in eastern Europe, was similar to one which slammed into a police cellblock south of Copenhagen on February 2, wounding a prominent Bandidos member but failing to go off.

They said the latest attack took place shortly after midnight, when the rocket hit a first floor cell, piercing the wall and flying through into the adjoining cell. The rocket failed to explode, the two prisoners were unhurt but both cells were wrecked.

The Bandidos and Hells Angels gangs, both offshoots of U.S. bike clans, have been battling over turf in Scandinavia since shortly after the Bandidos established themselves in the region in summer 1993.
The feud claimed its first life in February 1994, when a member of the Hells Angels-affiliated Rednecks died in a gunfight with Bandidos in the Swedish port of Helsingborg.
Two Bandidos died over the following two years, in Sweden and Finland, but on March 10 1996 the fighting took on a new intensity.

Gunmen outside Copenhagen International airport shot dead Danish Bandidos leader Uffe Larsen and wounded three of his companions as they waited to meet fellow-members returning from a visit to Helsinki.
A Copenhagen court, sitting in the tightest security ever seen in Denmark, jailed two Hells Angels for the killing in December.

A Danish Bandido was shot dead near the Norwegian city of Drammen in July and last October a missile ploughed into a party at the Hells Angels' Copenhagen headquarters, killing a gang member and a woman guest.

In another recent incident Hells Angel Kim Svendsen was killed on January 11 in the provincial town of Aalborg in what police believe was an act of revenge for the serious wounding of a Bandido in the town a month earlier.
